tone.target: fuzzy stoner rock crunch with big amp grind
tone.profile: fuzzy stoner rock crunch with big amp grind
tone.summary: A heavy, fuzzy stoner rock tone achieved using a Fuzz pedal into a powerful British amp model (UK 45 or UK 50) with a robust cabinet to deliver massive sustain and grind.

rig.name: Wolfmother - Joker And The Thief - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and excessive noise inherent in high-gain fuzz circuits.
blocks.gap: None. Standard practice for noisy rock tones.

blocks.purpose: Provide a gritty boost and slightly round out the upper mids before the main fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used here as a general dirty boost, simulating an early overdrive/boost pedal to push the signal into the fuzz. A dedicated Boost or OD 9 might be closer but Green OD offers better grit for stoner rock.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the core fuzzy texture and thick sustain required for stoner rock.
blocks.gap: None. Fuzz is explicitly requested over standard distortion.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the loud, aggressive breakup and mid-focused punch of a Marshall stack.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is chosen for its classic British rock aggression, fitting the 'big amp grind' requirement. While other amps are available, this model best captures the desired vintage hard rock tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the necessary physical cabinet tone and voicing to complement the UK 45 amp model.
blocks.gap: None. Standard pairing for British hard rock tones.

blocks.purpose: Slightly scoop the extreme frequencies to focus the sound and enhance the upper-mids for maximum riff punch.
blocks.gap: Used to fine-tune the aggressive tone. A simple EQ is necessary to prevent muddiness from the fuzz/amp combination.

blocks.purpose: Disabled. Chorus is explicitly avoided to maintain a dry, aggressive hard-rock attack.
blocks.gap: None. The module is included but deactivated based on the 'avoid' list.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and thickness without washing out the aggressive riffing.
blocks.gap: A small amount of room reverb is used to give 'big amp grind' depth, but kept low so it doesn't become a lead effect.

blocks.purpose: Final output level adjustment to ensure the tone is loud and impactful.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the desired Marshall-style punch and grit.

proposals.reason: Enhance the aggressive, mid-focused punch required for stoner rock.
